'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[2021 Uganda bombings]]
**Two children are killed by a bomb explosion at a village in [[Nakaseke District]]. The device looked like a [[jackfruit]] and was given to the children while they were playing. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/10/30/fruit-shaped-bomb-kills-two-children-in-uganda-police (Al Jazeera)]
*[[2021 Democratic Republic of the Congo attacks]]
**The [[CODECO]] and the Alliance for the Liberation of the Congo [[militia]] groups attack two villages in [[Ituri Province]], [[Democratic Republic of the Congo]], killing at least 14 [[civilian]]s. [https://punchng.com/14-dead-in-dr-congo-village-attack/ (AFP via ''The Punch'')]
*[[Afghanistan conflict (1978–present)|Afghanistan conflict]]
**Three people are killed and several injured when gunmen [[mass shooting|open fire]] at a wedding in [[Nangarhar]]. The [[Taliban]] are accused of being behind the attack, opening fire while music was being played. The Taliban has, however, said that the shooting was an internal dispute and that two of the attackers have been arrested. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2021/oct/30/gunmen-kill-at-least-three-at-afghan-wedding-to-stop-music-being-played (''The Guardian'')]
*[[Insurgency in the Maghreb]]
**Two employees of the Canadian [[mining industry of Mali|mining]] company [[Iamgold]] are reported missing following an attack on their convoy in [[Burkina Faso]] while travelling to [[Essakane]], [[Mali]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/canadian-mining-firm-iamgold-convoy-attacked-burkina-faso-several-missing-2021-10-29/ (Reuters)]
*[[Internal conflict in Myanmar]]
**[[Tatmadaw]] forces bombard the town of [[Thantlang]] in [[Chin State]], western [[Myanmar]], with [[artillery]] shells, destroying dozens of homes, after clashing with local self-defence forces who captured a soldier. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/10/29/myanmar-military-shells-restive-town-destroying-dozens-of-homes (Al Jazeera English)]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[Economy of Mexico]]
**The [[National Institute of Statistics and Geography]] in [[Mexico]] shows that the economy shrank 0.2% in the third-quarter from the three previous months and the [[GDP]] also declined during the same period of time, both largely due to the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on businesses. [https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/mexican-economy-shrinks-first-time-since-pandemic-rebound-2021-10-29/ (Reuters)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Oceania]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Australia]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Victoria]]
*****[[COVID-19 lockdown|Lockdown]] restrictions are further eased in [[Melbourne]] as 80% of the adult population are now [[COVID-19 vaccination in Australia|fully vaccinated]]. Schools, non-essential retail, restaurants and gyms reopen with density limits, masks are no longer mandatory outdoors, and travel between Melbourne and regional [[Victoria (Australia)|Victoria]] resumes. [https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/2021/oct/29/victorian-covid-restrictions-what-rules-and-regulations-are-changing-on-friday (''The Guardian'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Tonga]]
****[[Tonga]] reports its first case of [[COVID-19]] in a person who travelled from [[Christchurch]], [[New Zealand]] to [[Nukuʻalofa]] and is now in isolation. [https://www.rnz.co.nz/international/pacific-news/454525/covid-19-tonga-records-first-case (RNZ)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Andorra]]
****Minister of Culture and Sports [[Sílvia Riva González|Sílvia Riva]] tests positive for COVID-19. [https://www.diariandorra.ad/noticies/nacional/2021/10/29/silvia_riva_dona_positiu_per_covid_189398_1125.html (''Diari d'Andorra'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Poland]]
****[[Poland]] surpasses three million cases of COVID-19. [https://www.usnews.com/news/world/articles/2021-10-29/polands-total-number-of-covid-19-cases-passes-3-million (''U.S. News & World Report'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Russia]]
****[[Russia]] reports a record for the fourth consecutive day of 1,163 [[COVID-19 pandemic deaths|death]]s from COVID-19, bringing the nationwide death toll to 236,220. [https://abcnews.go.com/Health/wireStory/russia-marks-daily-deaths-record-infections-soar-80851892 (ABC News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Ukraine]]
****[[Ukraine]] reports a record for the second consecutive day of 26,870 new cases of COVID-19, bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 2.88 million. [https://www.reuters.com/article/health-coronavirus-ukraine-cases/-ukraine-reports-record-daily-high-of-26870-new-coronavirus-cases-ministry-idUKS8N2MT060 (Reuters)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in South America]]
***After seeing a slight increase in the number of cases and deaths, [[Chile]], [[Uruguay]] and [[Argentina]] intensify their [[vaccination]] rollouts. Chile has reported 37,719 total deaths from COVID-19 while Argentina has reported 115,916 total deaths from COVID-19. [https://www.elpais.com.uy/mundo/senales-aumento-casos-refuerzan-vacunacion-covid.html (''El País Uruguay'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Kyrgyzstan]]
***The [[Kyrgyzstan]] [[Cabinet of Ministers of the Kyrgyz Republic|Cabinet of Ministers]] issues a change of regulations that would require workers in the cultural, leisure, entertainment, and sport sectors to be [[vaccinate]]d against COVID-19 due to the ongoing [[pandemic]] situation in the country. [https://m.akipress.com/news:664117:Workers_of_culture_and_sport_in_Kyrgyzstan_required_to_get_vaccinated_against_COVID-19/ (AKIpress)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]], [[COVID-19 vaccination in the United States]]
***The [[Food and Drug Administration]] authorizes the [[Pfizer–BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine]] for children between the ages of 5 and 11, becoming the first vaccine to be approved for children in the [[United States]]. [https://www.cnbc.com/2021/10/29/pfizer-covid-vaccine-fda-authorizes-for-kids-ages-5-to-11.html (CNBC)]

'''International relations'''
*[[2021 Belarus–European Union border crisis]], [[Belarus–Poland relations]]
**The [[Senate of Poland]] approves a plan to construct an estimated {{Euro|353 million|link=yes}} ([[United States dollar|US$]]407 million) [[Border barrier|wall]] along [[Poland|the country]]'s [[Belarus–Poland border|border]] with [[Belarus]], in response to an influx of migrants. [https://www.barrons.com/news/polish-lawmakers-approve-belarus-border-wall-amid-migrant-influx-01635521408?tesla=y (AFP via ''Barron's'')]
*[[Moldova–Russia relations]]
**[[Moldova]] and [[Russia]]n [[Energy industry|energy firm]] [[Gazprom]] extend their supply contract, following accusations of Russia raising [[oil price]]s against Moldova. [https://www.themoscowtimes.com/2021/10/29/moldova-and-russia-extend-gas-contract-after-dispute-a75451 (AFP via ''The Moscow Times'')]
*[[Lebanon–Saudi Arabia relations]]
**[[Saudi Arabia]] recalls its ambassador to [[Lebanon]] and demands for Lebanon to [[Reciprocity (international relations)|reciprocate]] the action over "insulting" remarks about the [[Yemeni Civil War (2014-present)|war in Yemen]] made by Lebanese [[Ministry of Information (Lebanon)|information minister]] [[George Kurdahi]]. [https://www.rfi.fr/en/middle-east/20211029-saudi-recalls-envoy-to-lebanon-over-yemen-comments (AFP via RFI)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[LGBT rights in Afghanistan]], [[Treatment of women by the Taliban]]
**[[Taliban]]-appointed chief of the [[Central Bank of Afghanistan|Central Bank]] [[Shah]] Mehrabi says that [[gay rights]] will not be respected in [[Afghanistan]] because "That's against our [[Sharia]] law", but also said that, conversely, [[women's rights]] will be different than that of the 1990s. [https://news.trust.org/item/20211029082858-jijlg/ (Thomson Reuters Foundation)]
*Aftermath of the [[2021 Myanmar coup d'état]]
**U Win Htein, aide to the deposed Burmese leader [[Aung San Suu Kyi]], is sentenced to 20 years in prison for [[sedition]]. Htein became the first politician arrested in the aftermath of the February 2021 coup to be convicted. [https://www.dw.com/en/myanmar-suu-kyi-aide-jailed-for-20-years-for-treason-local-reports/a-59663450 (Deutsche Welle)]
*The [[European Parliament]] sues the [[European Commission]] for failing to properly enforce the [[Rule of Law Conditionality Regulation]] that is linked to the [[Next Generation EU]] recovery package, which refuses to fund [[Member state of the European Union|member states]] that fail to comply with the [[European Union]]'s [[rule of law]] standards. [https://edition.cnn.com/2021/10/29/europe/eu-parliament-sues-commission-rule-of-law-intl/index.html (CNN)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2025 Bangsamoro Parliament election|2022 Bangsamoro Parliament election]]
**[[President of the Philippines]] [[Rodrigo Duterte]] signs into law a bill postponing the [[Bangsamoro Parliament]] election to 2025. The interim government of [[Bangsamoro]] led by the [[Moro Islamic Liberation Front]] has requested the postponement due to the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic and the inability of the government to draw up an election code for the autonomous region. [https://www.straitstimes.com/asia/se-asia/philippines-postpones-self-rule-vote-in-restive-muslim-region (AFP via ''The Straits Times'')]

'''Science and technology'''
*[[Solar cycle 25]]
**An X-class [[solar flare]], the second of the current [[solar cycle]], erupts. An associated [[coronal mass ejection]] may graze Earth on October 30 or 31, which could cause bright [[aurora]]e and interfere with [[satellite communication]]s. [https://www.space.com/sun-unleashes-major-x-class-solar-flare-october-2021 (Space)]
